transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose... I'm just so worn out. Just walking from the bedroom to the kitchen, it feels like I've been hauling lumber all day. And resting doesn't give me anything back. I just sit there and it doesn't help. 

Hauling lumber... my uncle actually used to run a lumber yard. Down in Texas. I spent a summer there when I was taking some college classes, just stacking two-by-fours in the heat. He had this old hound dog named Buster that would just sleep under the office porch all day. Smart dog. Knew to stay out of the sun, unlike us. Uncle Pete ended up selling the place, though, back in '95 I think. Or maybe it was '96, right around the time the big hardware stores started moving into town and pricing everyone out. 

But... what was I saying? Oh, yeah. I just... I can't even make it to the kitchen to get a glass of water without feeling completely empty.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yeah, I guess so. It's just... I don't know. I used to love singing in the church choir, you know? Every Thursday night practice, Sunday morning service. And I'd play pickup basketball down at the community center on Tuesdays. I was always working on cars, too. My buddy Rick has this '68 Mustang we were restoring. Beautiful car. Cherry red. Well, it's going to be cherry red once it's painted. Right now it's mostly primer gray and rust. Rick's had that car since he was a teenager, bought it off his neighbor for practically nothing because the engine was shot. We spent three weekends just trying to source the right carburetor for it. 

But lately... I just can't make myself care. About the car, or the choir, or even grilling for the family on the weekends. I don't even answer Rick's texts anymore. Or anyone's texts, really. I just look at the phone and... I just don't care enough to type anything back.
Have you been feeling like you’re not worth much or that you’re a failure, or have you been blaming yourself for things that aren’t your fault?

Yeah... I do. I keep thinking about how I've just... completely failed my wife, and my kids, and my church. It honestly feels like every bad thing happening around us right now is just some kind of punishment for me not being the man I was supposed to be. 

The man I was supposed to be... you know, my dad was a real provider. He worked at the canning factory for thirty-five years. Never missed a single shift. Even when they had that big union strike back in '88, he was out there on the picket line every morning at 5 AM in the freezing cold. He had this heavy green Stanley thermos he took everywhere with him. Dropped it off the back of a pickup truck once on the highway and it just got a little dent in the side, kept the coffee boiling hot anyway. They really don't make things like that anymore, do they? Now you buy a toaster or a coffee maker and it's dead in a year. Just cheap plastic. My wife bought one of those fancy espresso machines last Christmas and it's already leaking all over the counter... 

But, um... what was the question? Right, feeling like a failure. Yeah. I just feel like I'm being punished for letting everybody down.
How often have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless during the past two weeks?

Every single day. I wake up and there's just this... this heavy, hopeless feeling right in the center of my chest. It's like I can't breathe right. Some days I don't even make it past the garage. I just go out there and sit on that old metal stool by the workbench and start crying, and I don't even know why. 

That stool, actually... I bought that at a garage sale down the street. Old Mrs. Higgins was clearing out her husband's things after he passed. He was a retired mechanic, had all these beautiful vintage Snap-on tools. I should have bought the socket set she had, but I just bought the stool. It's got this red vinyl seat that's cracked right down the middle, and one of the legs is a little shorter than the others so it wobbles if you don't sit on it just right. I tried fixing it once by gluing a piece of wood under the leg, but the glue didn't hold. Wood glue is funny like that, you really have to clamp it tight and leave it for a full 24 hours, and even then, if the surface isn't sanded right... 

Anyway. I just sit on that wobbly stool and cry. Every day. It just doesn't stop.
Have you had any thoughts about ending your life or that you’d be better off dead?

Yeah... yeah, I have. The thought just keeps coming that I should just be dead. That everyone would be better off. And when I'm alone in the house, it really scares me, because I start thinking I might actually do something to make that happen. 

I'm alone a lot during the day now since I'm not working. The house gets so quiet. Well, except for the refrigerator. It makes this loud humming noise, like a low buzz that kicks on every twenty minutes or so. I think the condenser coils in the back need to be vacuumed. You're supposed to do that twice a year, you know, pull it away from the wall and get all the dust bunnies out of the grate. If you don't, the compressor has to work twice as hard and it burns out the motor. My brother-in-law had that happen to his fridge right before Thanksgiving last year. They had a twenty-pound turkey in there and all the side dishes, and the whole thing just died. They had to pack everything into coolers with ice from the gas station. He tried to buy a new one on Black Friday but the delivery was backed up for three weeks... 

But yeah. When I'm alone with that humming noise... I just get so scared of what I might do to myself.
